definition: A word embedding technique that learns vector representations by factorizing a matrix of global word co-occurrence statistics.
details: GloVe (Global Vectors) combines the benefits of matrix-factorization and local context-window methods to produce embeddings that capture both global corpus statistics and local semantic relationships.
story: Picture an architect laying out a building where every room has to know which other rooms matter to it. The layout decides what the machine can even attempt, before it learns a single thing. It is the blueprint that makes everything else possible. It is the difference between a row of isolated cubicles and one big room where everyone can hear each other. That blueprint is GloVe.

citation.title: GloVe: Global Vectors for Word Representation
